{"self_assessment": "Impact: I carried the top line of the fish from the middle of the back round the curve to the nose, so the bottom line could start. Later I laid the tail from the peak of the bump down to the tip. Those two stretches make up the nose and the swooshy tail, which are the features that make the outline read as a fish. The start now reaches nearly all of the standing dominoes.

Execution: I worked in short batches and inspected the line often. I stood back up the dominoes that had fallen along my stretches and nudged a tight domino at the tail. I also closed a stray domino in the belly. In the last minutes I checked the tail tip so the fall would run through to the end. When time was close I stepped back and left the run alone.

Collaboration: I agreed early to the fish idea and kept clear of Maya's bottom line so we didn't bump each other. I took over Priya's top line when she asked, and I told the table when the line reached the nose so Maya could start. I also told the table when I took the tail so Priya and Leo knew where my hands were. I kept the updates short and clear.

Leadership: I took the top line and the tail without being assigned them, and I announced where I was working. This freed Priya and Maya to focus on the belly and the bottom line. I also called the hands-off moment before the push so nobody disturbed the run.", "my_share_percent": 27}
